OWL app, standalone and networked | Design review | 12 Oct 2026

One job per screen, readable from the cab

One design for the app, the standalone dashboard and the networked controller. The screens are cut back to what a farmer does with the tractor running: check the camera, spray, record, change settings and get the data off. New in this version: AI models and Hailo, Noktura in the app, tablet layouts and the networked controller.

  1. 1The camera is the first thing you see. Spraying is one big switch, not one of four equal toggles.
  2. 2Tabs have words under them. A farmer shouldn't have to guess what an icon means.
  3. 3Settings is a short list you tap into, not one long scrolling page.
  4. 4When something can't work, the screen says why and how to fix it. AI mode never quietly falls back to colour.
  5. 5Every target is at least 44 px, main actions are 54 px or more, and the colours are tuned for direct sun.

Phone app

Scroll sideways. Each screen is the new design. What it changes is written underneath.

AI models and Hailo

One page, four states. It always says what runs the AI, and never hides a model.

Noktura in the app

A Home card in three states, and a page behind it.

App on a tablet, or a phone turned sideways

The app switches layout by itself when the screen is 840 px or wider. Rotating keeps the same tab open.
